claim: The M5/M6 power grid is restored on the routed slice (issue #66) and measured. Power delivery in layout/pnr/slice.pnr.report.json is complete (1,016 VDD / 1,021 VSS STRIPE segments, 1,085/1,089 vias), up from the post-#64 partial state (0 stripe segments). The deck-prohibited families from the pre-#64 straps are all zero: V4.M5.AUX.2, M4.AUX.1/2/3 and M5.AUX.1/2/3 at both levels. Four residual families are NEW from the grid and are reported by name and count below; the grid is therefore NOT deck-clean and nothing here claims it is. The recipes' own documented V4 enclosure residuals are present as predicted by 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4499. First DRC run on the regenerated streams at the current pin (klt 0.9.2), same command form as the r4 record, full 267-id expectation set, nothing waived, filtered or relaxed: the packaged ASAP7 deck is unmodified, no --rules, no --waivers. Both runs completed; the summary-only envelopes are committed alongside this record and --check matches on the authoring host. Layout results against a predictive PDK, not measurements. Not T1 item 3 evidence: the manifest does not cite it and item 3 stays unmet. Not T1 item 10 evidence: none of the files this issue edits is a member of manifests/t1-item10-inventory.json (re-verified 2026-11-17), so the item-10 envelope is untouched.

request_change.what: power.straps gains the klt asap7sc7p5t recipe transcribed explicitly (M5 w 0.216 / p 5.4 / off 0.306 / sp 0.312; M6 w 0.288 / p 5.376 / off 0.344 / sp 0.096, after the unchanged M1/M2 followpin rails), and power.connects carries the recipe's two via-stack tunings (M2<->M5 max_columns 1 ongrid {M3 M4}; M5<->M6 max_columns 1). power_net/ground_net, the floorplan, the tracks and every other request field are unchanged.
request_change.why_preset_not_used: The shipped "power": {"preset": "asap7sc7p5t"} form cannot be combined with this request's post_route_spef/post_route_sdf: the preset validates pdk.cell_library as asap7sc7p5t_28 (exact match, measured verbatim error), while the post-route pass validates it as asap7sc7p5t_rvt, the only ASAP7 entry in the extract-deck table (second verbatim error, measured by also trying the renamed library). Dropping post_route_spef/sdf to use the preset verbatim would stale the committed post-route SDF that STA and SDF-annotated simulation consume. Filed generically as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#6029; the docs' explicit form is stated to be validated identically, which this run confirms (the request echoes the recipe's geometry and via tuning unchanged apart from the M5 offset below).
request_change.why_m5_offset_0p306: The deck's Mx.AUX.1 grids are absolute (offset 0 from the layout origin, asap7.drc GRID ORIGIN note), while pdngen strap offsets are core-origin relative. This floorplan's core origin x is 1.026 um (ROW ROW_0 x, 1026 nm = 18 mod 24), so the recipe's M5 offset 0.312 puts every M5 strap edge at 6 mod 24 nm - off the deck grid. Measured from the floorplan-stage DEF (pdngen runs at floorplan; strap centerlines extracted from SPECIALNETS): at offset 0.312 all eight M5 centerlines sat at 18 mod 24 nm (edges 6 mod 24); at 0.306 every M5 strap edge sits on the 24 nm grid. The envelope's M5.AUX.1 count of 0 is the committed-stream measurement of the same fact. The M6 offset 0.344 already lands every M6 strap edge on the 32 nm grid at this core origin (edges 0 mod 32, M6.AUX.1 = 0), so it is kept at the recipe value. The offset change is the minimal deck-grid correction of the recipe for this core origin; widths, pitch and spacing are the recipe's unchanged.

new_families_from_the_grid.note: Reported by name and count per the acceptance criteria. With these present, power delivery is complete but the grid is NOT deck-clean and no claim here says otherwise. Under --engine klayout every marker returns source_cell: null (2AMLogic/klayout-tools#5661), so the attributions below are from a marker-geometry study: a separate marker-bearing run on the slice (same deck, default cap, scratch envelope not committed) plus the floorplan-stage DEF of the same request.

V4.M4.EN.1.cause: The recipe's wide-V4 via bar (VIARULE M5_M4widePWR0p864, CUTSIZE 216x24) has zero M4 enclosure by design; the count equals the stack crossings exactly (648 = 2 nets x 324 stacks). Documented as inherent to the recipe by 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4499 ('the tech LEF's wide V4 bar has zero M4 enclosure ... no existing request field changes that'). Not re-filed.

V4.M5.EN.2.cause: Same recipe family: M5 enclosure of the wide V4 bar at 12 crossings. The tool PR measured ~13 on its much smaller block. Documented as inherent to the recipe by #4499. Not re-filed.

M3.S.2.cause: pdngen's M2<->M5 stack stub geometry: every marker sits inside an M5 strap column at a followpin-rail crossing, i.e. on the connect's own M3 patches, which can sit closer than the deck's 40 nm along-track spacing at some rail pitches. max_columns is already 1 and ongrid {M3 M4} is what the recipe is; the docs' split_cuts route is documented DRC-dirty (#4301). New at block scale - the tool PR measured 0 on its tiny block. Filed generically as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#6030.

M5.W.3.cause: Router, not pdngen: the violating shapes' across-track extents are 336/384/432 nm - even multiples of the 24 nm grid - and none aligns with a strap edge or the 216 nm strap width, so these are TritonRoute's own M5 via-landing patches widened under the strap-congested route (r4's strapless route produced 0). No place-and-route request field tunes router patch geometry. The tool docs note 1-2 M5.W.3 as a known recipe residual; the count here is larger because the family scales with routed area. Counted with the recipe residuals; no separate filing, as the docs already record the family as a known remainder of this recipe.
